newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen losing steam.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen losing steam.

text.p: Polish shares extended Thursday's gain but analysts said the mixed buying and selling after price fixing on Friday and continued low turnover suggested the market would lose steam next week.
The main market, currently at 15,572.8 points, had fallen near 15,000 points during this week's public offering of copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz before the current rebound.

"It seems current gains represent a speculative rebound -- the market was so oversold...and the turnovers don't suggest the gains happened along with significant money," said Grzegorz Cimochowski, an analyst at ING Baring Securities in Warsaw.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 2.4 percent to 15,572.8 points and turnover fell 20.7 percent to 154.3 million zlotys on both markets.
Analysts said the approach of both mid-summer and September's parliamentary elections would likely keep demand and the WIG index down in coming weeks.

This weekend shares in KGHM's domestic large-investor non-preferred tranche and domestic large-investor preferred tranche will be allotted at special bourse sessions from a minimum price of 19.5 zlotys.

Analysts said Bank Handlowy, up two percent to 41.3 zlotys, could rise again on Monday after having gained each session this week on the back of Monday's debut 8.3 percent above its 35-zloty issue price.
